en.name: Oat flour
en.summary: Oat flour keeps 2 months in the pantry and 4 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Oats are the fattiest of the common cereals, so it is the oil rather than anything microbial that decides when a bag is finished.
en.pantry: 2 months in an airtight container on a cool, dark, dry shelf. Oats carry noticeably more fat than wheat or rice, which is what makes oat flour taste rich and also what makes it a poor keeper. Commercial oats are usually kiln-dried or steamed, which deactivates the lipase enzyme that would otherwise break that fat down very quickly — but it does not stop plain oxidation, and a bag left warm and open goes stale in weeks. Fresh oat flour smells sweet and creamy; stale oat flour smells sharp, soapy or faintly of cardboard.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for oat flour. The fridge does slow the oil and is a sensible middle option for a bag you will use across a season, but only in a genuinely airtight container: oat flour is fine, light and very absorbent, and it will take up both moisture and fridge odours given the chance. Let the container warm to room temperature before you open it.
en.freezer: 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F), the sensible default for a big bag or for flour you grind yourself from rolled oats. Use an airtight tub or a double bag with the air pressed out, and label it. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that; what runs out is flavour, as the fat oxidises slowly even cold. Home-ground oat flour is more fragile than commercial, because grinding exposes fresh surfaces of fat — grind small batches and freeze what you do not use.
en.thawing: Bring the sealed container up to room temperature before opening so the flour does not take up condensation. Small amounts can go straight from frozen into a batter.
spoilage: A sharp, soapy or cardboard smell instead of a sweet, creamy one.
A bitter or metallic aftertaste in the finished bake.
Clumping or hard lumps, meaning moisture got in.
Webbing, larvae or small moths in the container.
tips: Grind your own in small batches; home-ground oat flour ages faster than commercial.
Store in an opaque airtight tub rather than the bag it came in.
Smell it before baking — rancidity arrives before the date does.
Freeze a new bag for a couple of days to deal with any weevil eggs.

faq.q: How long does oat flour last?
faq.a: 2 months in an airtight container in the pantry, or 4 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Why does oat flour go off faster than plain flour?
faq.a: Oats carry more fat than wheat, and fat oxidises. That is what gives an old bag its sharp, soapy smell.
Yes, 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Seal it airtight, label it, and let it come back to room temperature before opening.

zh.name: 燕麥粉
zh.summary: 燕麥粉密封放常溫可放 2 個月，−18 °C 冷凍是 4 個月。燕麥是常見穀類裡油脂最高的一種，所以決定一袋粉何時結束的是油脂，而不是任何微生物。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐、放陰涼避光乾燥的架子，2 個月。燕麥的脂肪含量明顯高於小麥或稻米，這讓燕麥粉嚐起來濃郁，也讓它不耐放。市售燕麥通常經過烘乾或蒸製，把那個會迅速分解脂肪的脂解酶滅掉——但那擋不住單純的氧化，一包又溫又敞著的粉，幾週內就走味了。新鮮燕麥粉聞起來甜、帶奶香；走味的則刺鼻、有肥皂味或淡淡紙板味。
zh.fridge: 燕麥粉沒有公布的冷藏期限。冷藏確實能拖慢油脂，對一季內用得完的份量是合理的折衷，但容器必須真正密封：燕麥粉細、輕、吸收力又強，只要有機會就會把水氣和冰箱的味道一起吸進去。開蓋前先讓容器回到室溫。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 4 個月；大包裝，或你自己用燕麥片磨的粉，這就是合理的預設。用密封罐或套兩層袋、壓出空氣，並貼標籤。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；先用完的是風味，因為脂肪在低溫下仍會慢慢氧化。自己磨的燕麥粉比市售的更脆弱，因為研磨會把新的脂肪表面暴露出來——請少量磨，用不完的冷凍起來。
zh.thawing: 整罐密封著回到室溫再開蓋，粉才不會受潮。少量的話直接從冷凍加進麵糊也沒問題。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、有肥皂味或紙板味，而不是甜甜的奶香。
成品帶苦味或金屬味的餘韻。
結塊或出現硬塊，表示受潮了。
容器裡出現絲網、幼蟲或小蛾。
tips: 自己磨就少量磨；自磨的燕麥粉比市售的老化得快。
用不透光的密封罐，不要就著原袋放。
烤之前先聞；油耗會比日期更早出現。
新買的整袋先冷凍兩三天，處理掉蟲卵。

faq.a: 密封放常溫 2 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 4 個月。

faq.q: 燕麥粉為什麼比一般麵粉更快壞？
faq.a: 燕麥的脂肪比小麥多，而脂肪會氧化。那就是老燕麥粉那股刺鼻肥皂味的來源。
可以，−18 °C 下 4 個月。密封、貼標籤，開蓋前先讓它回到室溫。
